market_name: Will Trump be impeached by end of 2026?

trade_eligibility.reason: Below minimum expected move or unclear direction.

time_plan.30m: Check whether the probability move coincides with a concrete news headline (formal filing of articles, defection of GOP members) vs. thin liquidity churn; check SPY futures tick.
time_plan.1h: Compare against VIX and Treasury futures — a real risk event would show up in vol, not just this one contract.
time_plan.2h: Assess whether mainstream wire services (AP, Reuters) are carrying the story; if not, treat as pre-public but low-conviction.
time_plan.6h: Re-evaluate whether the impeachment odds move is sustained or has reverted; check dollar index and gold for any risk-off confirmation.
time_plan.12h: Mark whether SPY realized any move beyond normal daily noise; log whether the political signal had any measurable asset impact for calibration.

predictions.reasoning: A House impeachment vote is a political/symbolic event with essentially zero probability of Senate conviction given the current GOP-leaning Senate math. Historically (Clinton 1998, Trump 2019 and 2021) impeachment proceedings produced negligible S&P 500 reaction — markets treat impeachment without removal as noise. A sharp move in this market's implied probability most plausibly reflects rising odds Democrats capture the House in the 2026 midterms, which is a slow-burn political story, not a same-day 12h catalyst. Any equity impact would be small and could cut either way (mild risk-off from governance uncertainty vs. gridlock being seen as status-quo/market-neutral).

evidence_used: Market resolves on House vote alone, no Senate conviction required — a low bar but still requires House majority
House impeachment currently requires a Democratic majority, effectively tying this market to 2026 midterm outcomes
Historical precedent: Clinton and both Trump impeachments produced minimal S&P 500 reaction
No specific tradable catalyst embedded in the question — it's a year-plus horizon political question
uncertainty_notes: A 12h window is far too short to capture the slow political process this market tracks
Direction of any equity impact is genuinely ambiguous — impeachment-without-removal has historically been market-neutral
This market is more a proxy for House control than for governance disruption
Move in implied probability could be liquidity noise on a low-volume political contract

llm_justification.summary: This market tracks whether the House passes articles of impeachment by end-2026 — a symbolic, low-consequence event given near-zero Senate conviction odds, and one effectively gated on Democrats winning the House in the 2026 midterms. The mapping to liquid public assets is weak: historically impeachment proceedings barely moved US equities, and the 12h window cannot capture a year-plus political process. Best-guess proxy is broad US equities (SPY) with unclear direction and small magnitude — well below the 700bp tradable threshold. This is explicitly a low-conviction, non-tradable mapping.
key_assumptions: Senate conviction remains implausible, so impeachment is symbolic and low-impact for markets
Historical market indifference to impeachment persists
A probability spike reflects political/midterm expectations rather than an imminent economic shock
failure_modes: The proxy (SPY) is only weakly exposed — impeachment historically doesn't move broad equities
Any information may already be public via polling/political news, so no leak edge
A sharp move could be thin-liquidity noise on a niche political contract rather than real signal
If a genuinely disruptive scenario emerged (e.g., linked to a broader crisis), direction and magnitude could differ substantially from this base case
llm_justification.why_not_ex_post: The card is timestamped, content-hashed, and never overwritten. Execution must reject any card created after an anomaly's trigger time.
